paper.title: WINA: Weight Informed Neuron Activation for Accelerating Large Language Model Inference
paper.affiliation: Renmin University of China; Microsoft; University of California, Berkeley; University of Wyoming; Zhejiang University; Nanyang Technological University
paper.source_of_truth: Accepted ICLR 2026 manuscript represented by the arXiv v2 LaTeX e-print and rendered PDF. Mathematical statements were cataloged from tex_arxiv/03_method.tex, tex_arxiv/appendix.tex, tex_arxiv/proof_lemma_3.1.tex, and tex_arxiv/proof_theorem_3.5.tex; the rendered PDF fixes equation, appendix, and page numbering.
paper.scope_note: The accepted paper has two headline theoretical results: a single-layer fixed-density top-K optimality lemma and a deep-linear-network upper-bound theorem. The main definitions are the dense/gated approximation objectives and the TEAL/WINA gate rules. Appendix A.2 also gives an SVD identity showing that right multiplication by the right-singular-vector matrix produces a column-orthogonal matrix. Experimental comparisons, runtime measurements, and sparsity-allocation procedures are empirical or algorithmic claims rather than self-contained mathematical theorems. For Theorem 3.2, the catalog preserves the authors' intended layerwise-separable upper-bound conclusion and makes the exact separability bridge a formalization obligation; the weakest concrete network hypotheses supporting that bridge will be determined during proof development.

items.label: Problem / Eq. (1)
items.name: Deep-network gated-output approximation objective

background_notation.G: a family of binary activation gates, one for each layer
background_notation.M(X | G): the output of the network with gates G applied

hypotheses: Each layer gate is a binary vector of the appropriate input dimension.
items.statement_informal: Choose binary activation gates across all layers to minimize the Euclidean deviation between the dense and gated network outputs.
items.statement_formal: Minimize ||M(X) - M(X | G)||_2 over G = {g^(1), ..., g^(L)} with each g^(l) in {0,1}^{n_l}.
items.proof_as_in_paper: This is the paper's optimization problem, not a proved proposition. The text notes that the complete input set X is generally unavailable and motivates a sampled approximation and a per-layer refinement.

lean.route_note: The Lean definition abstracts over the concrete network evaluator and squares the Euclidean objective, which preserves its minimizers.

items.label: Refined Problem / Eq. (2)
items.name: Single-layer gated-output approximation objective

background_notation.W: an m by n real weight matrix
background_notation.g ⊙ x: coordinatewise masking of x by g

hypotheses: W is an m by n real matrix.
items.statement_informal: Choose a binary mask whose linear-layer output best approximates the dense output.
items.statement_formal: Minimize ||W x - W(g ⊙ x)||_2 over g in {0,1}^n.
items.proof_as_in_paper: This is the per-layer optimization problem obtained from Eq. (1), not a proved proposition.

lean.route_note: A gate is represented by its retained-coordinate finset. The objective is squared, without changing the optimization problem.

items.label: Eq. (3)
items.name: Magnitude-only top-K activation gate
hypotheses: A deterministic tie-breaking convention is fixed if boundary magnitudes tie.
items.statement_informal: Retain the K input coordinates with largest absolute magnitudes.
items.statement_formal: Set g_i = 1 exactly on a size-K set of indices attaining the K largest values of |x_i|, and set g_i = 0 elsewhere.
items.proof_as_in_paper: This is the gate used by the magnitude-only baselines discussed in the paper; no proof is claimed.

lean.route_note: The set-valued top-K predicate accepts every valid boundary tie choice rather than imposing an unprinted tie-breaker.

items.label: Eq. (4)
items.name: Weight-informed top-K activation gate

background_notation.c_i: the Euclidean norm ||W_{:,i}||_2 of column i of W

hypotheses: A deterministic tie-breaking convention is fixed if boundary scores tie.
items.statement_informal: Retain the K coordinates with largest products of input magnitude and weight-column norm.
items.statement_formal: Set [g_WINA]_i = 1 exactly on a size-K set attaining the K largest values of |x_i c_i|, where c_i = ||W_{:,i}||_2, and set it to zero elsewhere.
items.proof_as_in_paper: This is WINA's gate definition; no proof is claimed.

lean.route_note: Lean uses the squared nonnegative score x_i^2 ||W_{:,i}||_2^2, whose ordering is equivalent to the paper's absolute weighted score, and treats top-K ties set-valuedly.

items.label: Lemma 3.1 / Eq. (6)
items.name: Single-layer fixed-density WINA optimality under column orthogonality

background_notation.W: an m by n real matrix
background_notation.K: the target number of retained coordinates
background_notation.g_WINA(x): a size-K gate retaining the largest |x_i c_i| scores

hypotheses: W^T W is diagonal, equivalently the columns of W are pairwise orthogonal.
K is a positive integer with K < n.
The intended optimization domain consists of gates with exactly K active coordinates.
items.statement_informal: Among all gates retaining exactly K coordinates, WINA minimizes the single-layer output error by retaining the K largest weighted coordinates.
items.statement_formal: If W^T W is diagonal and g_WINA has exactly K ones at indices with the K largest values of |x_i| ||W_{:,i}||_2, then for every g in {0,1}^n with sum_i g_i = K, ||W x - W(g_WINA ⊙ x)||_2 <= ||W x - W(g ⊙ x)||_2.
items.proof_as_in_paper: Expand the squared error as ||sum_{i in I} x_i W_{:,i}||_2^2 = sum_{i in I} x_i^2 ||W_{:,i}||_2^2 + sum_{i != j in I} x_i x_j W_{:,i}^T W_{:,j}. Column orthogonality makes every cross term zero, so the error is the sum of squared weighted scores over omitted coordinates. WINA omits the n-K smallest |x_i c_i| scores and therefore reaches the lower bound, yielding Eq. (6).
items.proof_technique: Orthogonal norm expansion followed by finite top-K exchange/minimum argument.
items.proof_completeness: self-contained after restoring the fixed-density domain stated in the surrounding prose
known_issues_in_paper: The displayed argmin in Lemma 3.1 and Eq. (6) omits the exactly-K restriction already fixed by the surrounding prose and WINA gate definition. The formal statement restores that intended domain.

Appendix A.7 defines the omitted set as {i | x_i = 0}; the expansion uses the indices zeroed by the gate. It also calls the deterministic squared error an expected deviation, although orthogonality removes cross terms pointwise.
items.formalization_notes: State the theorem over finite index sets and size-K retained sets. Prove the exact omitted-score identity first, then use a finite exchange or top-K characterization. Treat ties extensionally: any size-K set satisfying the top-K order condition is optimal.

added_hypotheses: The optimization domain is restricted to gates retaining exactly K coordinates, as specified by the surrounding prose and gate definition but omitted from the displayed argmin.
lean.route_note: The proof follows Appendix A.7: rewrite the error using omitted coordinates, cancel cross terms through the diagonal Gram matrix, and apply a tie-safe finite top-K exchange argument.

items.label: Theorem 3.2
items.name: Deep-network WINA optimality for a separable upper bound

background_notation.M(x): the dense L-layer linear network W^(L)...W^(1)x
background_notation.G: the family of binary layer gates
background_notation.M^(l): the diagonal matrix formed from the gate g^(l), applied to the input of layer l
background_notation.k_l: the intended fixed number of coordinates retained at layer l

hypotheses: The linear maps have compatible finite dimensions and L >= 2 for the proof's inductive presentation.
For every layer l >= 2, W^(l)T W^(l) is diagonal.
Each layer gate is binary and, as intended by the top-k rule, has a fixed target cardinality k_l.
alpha > 0 for the particular Young upper bound constructed in Appendix A.8.
items.statement_informal: The paper claims that WINA's layerwise weighted top-K choices minimize a separable upper bound on the output deviation of a deep linear network.
items.statement_formal: The paper states that there exists a separable U such that E(x;G) <= U(x;G) for every admissible fixed-density gate family G and G_WINA belongs to argmin_G U(x;G). Appendix A.8 defines, at each decomposition step, U_alpha = (1+alpha)||u||_2^2 + (1+1/alpha)||v||_2^2 and claims WINA minimizes it recursively.
items.proof_as_in_paper: For two layers, decompose the gated-minus-dense error exactly as e_g = v + u, where v = W^(2)(M^(2)-I)W^(1)M^(1)x and u = W^(2)W^(1)(M^(1)-I)x. Expand ||e_g||_2^2 = ||u||_2^2 + ||v||_2^2 + 2 u^T v. The proof correctly notes that the cross term depends on the gates. Young's inequality gives 2 u^T v <= alpha ||u||_2^2 + alpha^{-1} ||v||_2^2, hence E <= U_alpha := (1+alpha)||u||_2^2 + (1+alpha^{-1})||v||_2^2. It then asserts that both norm terms have separable top-K forms and that WINA minimizes U_alpha. For N+1 layers it repeats the decomposition, observes that the new-layer v term is a weighted omitted-coordinate sum, and asserts that the u term is minimized recursively on the first N layers, concluding by induction.
items.proof_technique: Exact layerwise error decomposition plus Young's inequality and a claimed recursive top-K minimization.
items.proof_completeness: The exact decomposition and Young upper-bound step are self-contained. The recursive minimization step requires an explicit gate-independent separable-score representation; deriving that representation from concrete network assumptions remains a formalization obligation.
external_dependencies: Young's inequality 2 u^T v <= alpha ||u||_2^2 + alpha^{-1} ||v||_2^2 for alpha > 0.
known_issues_in_paper: The theorem statement does not formally define 'separable.' Appendix A.8's concrete Young bound contains later residuals that depend on earlier gates, so an explicit gate-independent separability bridge is needed for the stated joint minimization argument.

The theorem writes G_WINA = argmin_G U although argmin is set-valued, and it does not put the per-layer fixed-cardinality constraints in the displayed optimization domain. The formal statement uses membership in argmin over the top-k domains intended by the surrounding text.

The two-layer proof writes ||A(M^(1)-I)x||_2^2 as a sum of omitted squared column scores for A=W^(2)W^(1). This identity needs orthogonality of the relevant effective columns (or equivalent cross-term cancellation), which is not immediate from diagonality of W^(2)T W^(2).

For a fixed incoming gated activation, the newest-layer residual is a top-k omitted-coordinate sum. This conditional layerwise fact is weaker than joint minimization over every gate family, because the incoming activation itself depends on earlier gates.
items.formalization_notes: Preserve the authors' route as three later proof obligations: the exact gated-error decomposition, the Young upper bound, and the separability-to-top-k minimizer implication. Candidate source-faithful repairs to investigate are: (a) an explicit gate-independent omitted-score representation as an additional hypothesis; (b) stronger orthogonality of the relevant effective products, such as A^T A diagonal for the two-layer first residual, together with a separate condition removing inter-layer gate dependence; or (c) the weaker conclusion of conditional per-layer top-k optimality rather than joint argmin optimality. Vanishing of the Young cross term alone does not resolve gate coupling. Any assumption or weakened conclusion absent from the paper must remain explicit.

added_hypotheses: Every layer gate is restricted to its fixed target cardinality, as intended by the paper's top-k rule but omitted from the displayed joint argmin.

The paper-facing joint-minimizer theorem assumes that the upper bound has a gate-independent separable omitted-score representation with nonnegative layer coefficients; Appendix A.8 does not derive this bridge from the printed diagonal-Gram hypotheses.

The concrete two-layer repair assumes diagonal Gram for the effective product W^(2)W^(1), that the first WINA gate is top-k for its effective scores, and that the WINA second gate makes the newest residual vanish.
lean.route_note: Lean mechanizes the paper's exact two-layer and N+1 decompositions, proves the scaled Young inequality rather than taking it as a premise, derives each valid omitted-score identity under its exact Gram condition, and proves the joint top-k conclusion conditionally from the explicit separability bridge. A separately named two-layer theorem gives a sufficient repair for the concrete Young objective, and an exact two-coordinate identity-network witness proves that its hypotheses are jointly satisfiable.

items.label: Appendix A.2 / Eq. (5)
items.name: Right-singular-vector transformation gives orthogonal columns

background_notation.W = U Sigma V^T: a singular value decomposition of W

hypotheses: W = U Sigma V^T is an SVD.
U and V are orthogonal matrices.
Sigma is diagonal with compatible dimensions.
items.statement_informal: Multiplying a matrix by its right-singular-vector matrix produces a matrix whose Gram matrix is diagonal.
items.statement_formal: If W = U Sigma V^T and W_hat = W V, then W_hat = U Sigma and W_hat^T W_hat = Sigma^T Sigma (written Sigma^2 in Eq. (5)); hence the columns of W_hat are mutually orthogonal.
items.proof_as_in_paper: Substitute W = U Sigma V^T and V^T V = I into W_hat = W V to obtain W_hat = U Sigma. Then W_hat^T W_hat = Sigma^T U^T U Sigma = Sigma^T Sigma, which is diagonal.
items.proof_completeness: self-contained for the matrix Gram identity; full transformer-level computational invariance is attributed to external work and Algorithm 1
external_dependencies: The model-level computational-invariance transformation is attributed to SliceGPT (Ashkboos et al., 2024); Eq. (5) itself needs only standard SVD identities.
known_issues_in_paper: For rectangular matrices, the diagonal Gram factor is Sigma^T Sigma; the notation Sigma^2 in Eq. (5) is dimensionally literal only under the paper's square/compatible-diagonal convention.
items.formalization_notes: Formalize the Gram identity as a notation bridge from the paper's SVD symbols to Mathlib's matrix multiplication and transpose operations. Keep the broader model-invariance algorithm separate unless its companion transformations are fully specified.

lean.route_note: The paper-notation bridge assumes the stated SVD factorization and orthogonality identities, proves the rectangular Gram factor Sigma^T Sigma, and derives its diagonal Gram matrix from the paper's literal square-diagonal Sigma convention. The rectangular theorem exposes diagonal Sigma^T Sigma as the dimensionally precise condition.
